raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's chili.

I'm 56 now, been working this land for 37 years. My wife and I live on it, the kids have their own work in town. We only have 2 mu — it's not much, but chili brings in more money per mu than wheat or maize ever did, so that's why I stick with it. Labor is mostly just me and my wife; I'm not as quick as I used to be, but 2 mu of chili, we can handle it ourselves if we pace ourselves through picking season.

**What I'm planning:**

I'll buy seedlings from the nursery in Quzhou town again, same place as the past few years — about 3,500 plants per mu, the red long-chili variety that the traders pay decent money for. Raising my own seedlings is too much trouble for just 2 mu, and the nursery ones are healthier anyway. I'll lay down the black mulch film after I put in the base fertilizer — keeps weeds down and holds moisture, and at my age I don't want to be hoeing all summer.

Transplanting around the last week of April, once the cold snap is past. Middle of June is when the first flowers set — that's when I have to watch the water carefully. If you let the soil dry out at fruit set, yield drops bad, I learned that the hard way back around 2010 or so.

**Fertilizer:** For the base, I spread about 2 cart-loads of chicken manure I get from the poultry farm down the road (cheap, and chili likes it), plus about 40 kg of compound 15-15-15 per mu worked in before transplanting. Then I topdress urea twice during fruiting — maybe 10 kg per mu each time — through the drip or just side-dressed with the irrigation. The extension guy last year told me to use more potash for fruit quality so I'll throw in some potassium sulfate this year, maybe 10 kg/mu, see if the peppers color up better.

**Water:** I've got the well, electricity meter on it. I irrigate right after transplanting, then about every 10-15 days depending on rain. Usually 6 or 7 times total across the season. Costs me maybe 60-80 yuan a mu in electricity over the year.

**Pests:** Aphids show up every year, and if it's humid, anthracnose can hit the fruit and ruin a whole picking. I spray 3-4 times — usually an insecticide for aphids and thrips, a fungicide a couple of times. I buy the cheaper generics from the agri-shop in town, they work fine.

**Picking:** Starts end of July, goes through September, sometimes into early October. We pick every 7-10 days. My wife does most of the picking, I do the hauling. If prices are good, we pick more often; if traders aren't offering much, we let them ripen more and dry them ourselves.

**What I expect:** A normal year, we get around 2500 kg fresh off these 2 mu, or if we dry a lot, about 500 kg dry. Market price moves around a lot — last year was decent, year before was bad. I don't borrow, I pay cash for all the inputs. If the year's bad, we still have the off-farm money, that's why I can afford to keep farming this little plot.
